title: Starting a blog!
text:
Scientific debate currently revolves around papers, being the agreed upon way to make science, but they can’t be the only outlet for scholarly discussion. Post-publication review is still mostly theory, and post-publication is often severely lacking. Response articles exist, but usually you don’t want to go through months of peer review unless it’s something really big, and it seems more of a way to get into an academic fight than anything at times.
So, what do we have? Conferences are one option, but they involve a restricted number of people at one specific time. Mostly, the discussion of published material involves some off-handed comments while referencing it, lost in the body of a text. And then there’s the blog, this old-fashioned way to use the internet.
I’m not ashamed to say that I have learnt more from some posts on blogs such as those in resources than from some papers. Inspired by those and others, I decided to start a blog, in the hope of doing a bit of the same myself. Posts could be small ideas, or just practical examples. Some of the latter come from my own work, where they might have been small technicalities, shadowed by the bigger goal and message, which could be of broader interest despite their simplicity.
I have focused a lot on discussion, and surely there is the possibility of real-time discussion, as allowed by the internet, but I also intend this in the broader terms: publishing something for people to read and benefit from is already part of a discussion. So, I’m happy to write about what I like to do in a less formal way, and you’re welcome to just read the incoming posts, maybe benefit from them or even acknowledge the help!
Have a nice stay here.

title: About
text:
Hi! I’m Luciano. Currently, I’m a PhD student at the University of Camerino, working on a thesis on plant traits and functional diversity at small scales. My interests are ecology, statistics and software, in particular trait-based ecology, Bayesian models, causal inference, and R.
This blog is an outlet for helpful ideas, technical aspects, and discussions that might come up during my work or while reading, and don’t quite fit into conventional academic outlets. Sometimes maybe they do, but tucked away in some corner because not everyone is a curious nerd.

Books

Statistical Rethinking, 2nd ed., such a great book to learn more about statistical models and Bayes, or even just to refine one’s scientific approach. Calling it a methods book is reductive, calling it a science book is too vague. The writing is captivating, the approach is innovative. A convincing synthesis of Bayesian models and causality that has won me over
Numerical Ecology, 3rd ed., a bit old fashioned, and I think there’s a bit too much focus on testing and significance, but still a staple collection of the fundamental numerical methods in ecology
